entity.description: The Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo is home to a richly diverse and decidedly unique population of animals for a small-town community zoo. With 118 species and 22 critically endangered species, every animal has a name and a backstory. The zoo is committed to education, conservation, adventure, and community engagement. Located in Gulf Shores, Alabama, the zoo offers daily keeper presentations, animal adventures, and premium animal experiences.

Adults (ages 13-54) are $23.95, seniors (62+) and military are $20.95, children (ages 3-12) are $15.95, and children 2 and under are free. Prices do not include tax.

Yes, the zoo offers strollers, double strollers, and wagons to rent. We also offer complimentary manual wheelchairs available on a first-come, first-serve basis. A mobility scooter is available to rent for $20.

Yes, our Animal Adventures are a very popular and unique educational zoo program. All children under age six must be accompanied by a paying adult (which can include a sibling age 13 or older). The price of each adventure varies, but children, age two and under, are free.

Yes! Please view our Groups page or call 251-256-7008 for more information.

Yes, the zoo is ideal for any celebration. We also offer a few zoo party perks to add to your special occasion. Find out more about private parties. or call us on 251-256-7008

Yes, we love educating schoolchildren about wildlife and conservation. Our tax-exempt school, church, or civic group program offers an affordable and unique learning opportunity. Learn more on our Groups Page!

All zoo guests, age 15 and under, must be chaperoned by someone at least 16 years old who is also a paying zoo guest.

Our zookeepers love educating visitors about the animals. They offer keeper presentations at various times and locations throughout the park. Our highly entertaining, educational animal stage shows are presented daily during the warm-weather months.

Our current Keeper Presentation Schedule:

Yes, the gift shop is also the main entrance to the zoo and where admission tickets are sold. However, you do not have to buy a ticket to shop for merchandise in our store. We sell a great variety of animal-themed items, from clothing and jewelry to toys and books. 

Yes. Drink machines, mini melt ice cream, and snow cones are available inside the Zoo. A Micro Market is open inside The Manor, near the Lemur Adventure. It will offer self-serve convenience-type foods and snacks.

Guests are allowed to bring food into the zoo. Drink machines, mini melt ice cream, and snow cones are available inside the Zoo. A Micro Market is open inside The Manor, near the Lemur Adventure. It offers self-serve convenience-type foods and snacks.

Smoking any kind, including electronic or vape cigarettes, pipes, and cigars, is not permitted anywhere on the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo grounds.We do not allow zoo guests to carry any firearms inside the zoo grounds.

To ensure the safety of all animals, yours and ours, please keep your pets at home, and please do not keep them locked up in your vehicle while visiting the zoo.

Service dogs are permitted in the park by the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). However, to ensure the safety of our guests and our animals, and the visiting service dog, certain precautions must be followed.

We encourage guests to take photos for their enjoyment. However, as a non-profit organization, it is strictly prohibited to commercially use, or reproduce in any form, photography of our facility, animals, staff, or any zoo events that take place at off-site venues, without prior written permission from the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo.

Yes, we do. A zoo membership is also an exciting gift for families or employees.

Yes, whether you’re a resident or live out of state, you can participate in the care and feeding of a favorite zoo animal or the upkeep of a zoo exhibit through our sponsorship programs. Please call 251-256-7008 ext 124 and  for more info.

There are many options to provide much-needed support to our non-profit zoo. You can become a “Friend of the Zoo” and hold a fundraising event, sponsor one of our educational programs, participate in “Leave a Legacy,” or simply make a cash contribution. All donations and support programs may be tax-deductible. The Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo is a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization. Learn more about supporting the zoo on our Support Page.

Destination Madagascar

While visiting Destination: Madagascar, you are transported into the home of our black and white ring tailed lemurs. You will have the opportunity to meet these unusual animals from the Island of Madagascar and learn about their environment. Join us at Destination: Madagascar to learn more about these critically endangered animals.

South American Adventure

In the South American Adventure, you will walk along a boardwalk in the “jungle” to discover and meet a variety of animals from the tropical rainforests of Central and South America. During this adventure, you will learn about tortoises, macaws, sloths, and the importance of tropical forests in our everyday lives. Join us for a South American Adventure!

Feedings

Did you know the word “twiga” means giraffe in Swahili?  At the Twiga Station, you can meet our giraffes, learn about them, and have a chance to feed one of them!  These gentle giants eat as much as 70 pounds of leaves a day.  Help the keepers by feeding the giraffes various types of browse.  Be sure to check out their amazingly long tongues!

South American Adventure!
Come ~hang out~ with our sloths

In the South American Adventure, you will walk along a boardwalk in the “jungle” to discover and meet a variety of animals from the tropical rainforests of Central and South America. During this adventure, you will learn about tortoises, macaws, sloths, and the importance of tropical forests in our everyday lives. Plus, you may get to interact with our sloths… up close and personal! Join us for a South American Adventure!

Photo Gallery
Tickets

Appropriate for all ages, each adventure ticket is $24.95 per person, plus a regular paid zoo admission. Tickets can be purchased in the park on the day of your visit. Open to all ages. Children under age 10 must be accompanied by a paying adult. No reservations are needed. Adventures are done on a first-come, first-serve basis.

BUY ZOO TICKETS
Things to know:
WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT DURING YOUR ADVENTURE

Guests are taken in throughout the day in 20-minute intervals. Groups of up to 6 people are taken into the adventure at one time. This is a keeper-supervised adventure, and to ensure that it’s a safe and enjoyable experience for our guests, our keepers, and most especially, our sloths, we reserve the right to make last-minute decisions regarding the group size of the visit.

Sloths are not able to be held. The adventure area is handicap accessible. Service animals are not allowed in the exhibit.

The exhibit is in a shaded, outdoor enclosure; however, if the weather conditions are questionable, please call ahead to check if we are still selling tickets. Adventures are not available if there is lightning in the area or if it’s storming. The level of interactions are dependent on the animal’s temperament and interest in participation.

The feeding area is handicap accessible. No service animals are allowed in the station.

The station is in a shaded outdoor enclosure; however, if the weather conditions are questionable, please call ahead to check if we are still selling tickets. Feedings are not available if there is lightning, heavy rain, or freezing temperatures. Sulcata Tortoise Feeding
Sulcata Tortoise Feeding
10:30-11:30 and 2:30-3:30 Daily

Come join us for the Sulcata Tortoise Feeding at Coola Springs! You will have the opportunity to meet and learn more about this amazing keystone species from the Savanna. Visit them at their yard, offer them a yummy snack of leafy greens, and have the opportunity to touch their shell.

Photo Gallery
Tickets

Each adventure feeding is $5 per person, plus regular admission. Tickets can be purchased in the park on the day of your visit. Minimum age is 5 years old. Children under 10 must be accompanied by a paid adult. No reservations are made. Adventure is done on a first come first serve basis. There is limited availability. Closed-toe shoes are recommended but not required.

GET ZOO TICKETS
Things to know:
WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT FOR YOUR ECOUNTER

This is a keeper supervised feeding to ensure that it’s a safe and enjoyable experience for our guests, our keepers, and most importantly our tortoises. Groups of up to 6 people are taken to the tortoise yard at one time.

We reserve the right to make last-minute decisions regarding the group size of the visit. Animal feedings and the level of interactions are dependent on the animal’s temperament and interest in participation. The adventure area is handicap accessible. Service animals are not allowed in the exhibit. 

The exhibit is in an open outdoor enclosure, if the weather conditions are questionable, please call ahead to check if we are still selling tickets. Feeding is not available if there is lightning, heavy rain, or freezing temperatures.

Premium Experiences

The Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo is now offering exclusive premium experiences on select days. These experiences include the following:

Big Cat Premium Experience – $350 (includes 4 people)

A 45-minute experience behind the scenes with the carnivore department. Guests (up to
4 people, age 10 and over) will watch a training session with our large cats, provide
treats, help prepare diets and learn more about the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo lions, lynx,
serval, and clouded leopards. The Big Cat Experience does not allow hands-on contact with any cat. A protective barrier fence will be between guests and the animals at all times. Available on Thursdays.

Giraffe Premium Experience – $350 (includes 4 people)

A 45-minute experience behind the scenes with Giraffes Benjamin and Akayla along with
their Ostrich friends Netty, Poppy, and Clover. Guests (up to 4 people, all ages welcome)
will watch, learn, and help feed the giraffe their afternoon diets and explore inside the giraffe barn. Available on Mondays.

 

All premium experiences are offered on select dates. Each experience must be booked one week in advance. Select buy tickets below to see dates.

BIRTHDAY PARTIES AT ALABAMA GULF COAST ZOO
Creating Memorable Moments: The Ultimate Zoo Birthday Package Experience

The birthday package at the zoo includes a gift for the birthday child, all-day admission, and hay cups for barn animals. Parties are held for a 3 hour time slot in a reserved area inside the zoo.

The schedule includes wristband distribution, pizza, water, and a cookie cake. Pre-approved decorations are permitted, but balloons and certain items are prohibited for animal safety. The guest count includes the birthday child, siblings, parents, and all other guests, with children under 2 being exempt.

Booking Details:
Must be booked a full 2 weeks before the requested date to be assured full accommodation
Parties available 7 days a week at 9:30am and 1:00pm
Parties are not considered booked until a 50% non-refundable deposit has been paid
Final count and final payment due 3 days prior to party date
$415 for Non-Members or $375 for Members (per group up to 15) plus tax
Additional guests (after first 15) are $16.50 plus tax each
Includes:
Reserved Space (outdoor venue) for up to 3 hours
Admission for 15 people (adults and children over 2)
Pizza and water 
Cookie cake 
Paper Products (plates & napkins)
Hay cups for the barn animals
Unlimited carousel rides
CALL TO BOOK BIRTHDAY PARTY

Bouncy House Rental-3 hours $125
Animal ambassador visit to your party $50 (choose between fur, feathers, or scales) Animal ambassadors will arrive at the beginning of the scheduled party time and stay approximately 30 minutes.

LEARN WITH US
Inspiring Education & Conservation

What better way to learn about animals and how we humans can become better stewards of Earth’s wildlife than visiting a zoo? The animals of the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo are the cornerstone and inspiration for every educational program we offer.

With over 200 animals, there couldn’t be better learning opportunities: for families, school groups, and community or organization events for anyone interested in the wonderful creatures we share this planet with.

Avenues For Learning
School Groups &
Educational Programs

Bring your classroom to the wild with our School Groups & Educational Programs at the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo! Our free curriculum-based lesson plans provide students with hands-on learning opportunities that spark curiosity and inspire a love for wildlife.

Reserve your educational adventure today and turn learning into an unforgettable experience!

Zoo History

The mission of the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo is to create compelling experiences that connect people and community with wildlife, and inspire personal responsibility for conservation of the natural world. Education. Conservation. Adventure. Community.

1989

Gulf Shores, Alabama entrepreneur Joey Ward builds a small, community zoo on a family-owned parcel of land in the heart of town, a mile from the beach. Zooland Animal Park becomes home to a collection of tropical birds, snakes, big cats and other exotic wildlife, run by a small staff of zookeepers. While Zooland is extremely popular with locals and vacationers, Gulf Shores isn’t the tourist hot spot it is today, and the zoo is only a seasonal attraction. However, Joey and his parents, Wade and Pat Ward, are devoted custodians of the zoo’s animals.

1991

The Ward family forms a non-profit charitable organization, The Zoo Foundation, Inc. to operate the park, and the Wards continue their generosity and dedication to the zoo.

1995

Alabama transplant Patti Hall walks through the gates of the zoo to become a volunteer. Her passion for animals and professional credentials in management, administration, education and public communications puts her on a path that will dramatically change the zoo’s fate forever.

1997

Joey Ward and the Zoo Board of Directors asks Patti Hall to take over as Zoo Director. The following year, while running a zoo now filled with hundreds of animals, Patti faces her first big challenge living on the Gulf Coast, with the arrival of Hurricane Georges. Realizing that yearly tropical storm season is a new way of life, her dedication to the zoo’s animals means that their safety and security takes precedence over everything else. Little does she know the true test she will face a few years later.

1999

Patti hires Cyndi Johnson as Head Zookeeper who will later become the zoo’s Curator. Patti’s primary responsibility is to keep the zoo operational and open during tourist seasoning in order to make enough money during the spring and summer months to survive through fall and winter, the off-season. She holds raffles, bake sales, even raids zoo vending machines to pay the bills, feed and care for the animals and stay operational.

2000

Patti and the Board decide to rename the zoo to bring more credibility and prestige to the organization. The Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo is officially born. Each tourist season, Patti launches various zoo programs, including: educational animal visits to schools and libraries, community events, and promotions aimed at tourists. She turns “Boo in the Zoo” into a monster Halloween hit drawing over 2,500 annual attendees, and makes many improvements to animal exhibits, the gift shop, and the facility grounds.

2004

By the end of summer, the zoo has its best season ever. Then, an unbelievable twist hits the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo and turns its world upside down and inside out. On Monday, September 13th, CBS news anchor Dan Rather announces that a deadly Category 3 hurricane named Ivan is heading toward the Alabama coast. Gulf Shores will likely be the bullseye, and a mandatory evacuation has been ordered for thousands of residents. But what about hundreds of zoo animals?

2004- Continued

Patti is certain they will not survive the deadly storm if they are left behind. No US zoo has ever been completely evacuated for a natural disaster, until the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo. Over 36 hours, Patti and her staff pack up over 265 animals and transport them 20 miles inland to her home and property where they, her staff’s families, and their pets, all hunker down to wait out Hurricane Ivan. There is one animal they must leave behind - the zoo’s mascot, Chuckie, the 11-ft. 1,000 lb. American alligator who they hope will survive in his swampy exhibit.

2004- Continued

On September 16th, Hurricane Ivan makes landfall. The Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo is completely destroyed and under 14 feet of water from the Gulf of Mexico. The towns of Gulf Shores and Orange Beach are also demolished. In the aftermath back at Patti’s house, there is no municipal power or running water, cell and telephone service are down, and they have a very limited supply of food and bottled water for the staff and the animals.

2004- Continued

They are completely dependent on a few small generators and cut off from all emergency services. The temperature and humidity are in the high 90’s to add to the misery. In spite of the direness, they had all survived the worst natural disaster to hit the Gulf Coast in 25 years. Yet, the animals of the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo are now all homeless, and Patti’s staff has no idea if their own homes are still standing. But not one animal life is lost in the transport or during the relocation, and no zookeeper has been injured, except for Patti who received a monkey bite on her finger. The bond between animals and keepers during this extraordinary undertaking is beyond description.

2004- Continued

In the aftermath of Hurricane Ivan, word spreads about Patti’s historic rescue mission and for the zoo’s desperate search for Chuckie, the alligator who has gone missing. The national media comes calling. NatGeo, People magazine, The Weather Channel, CNN, Good Morning America, local TV and radio stations and countless newspapers report on and interview Patti. Lifting their spirits, Chuckie is found safe and sound, and this little zoo in Alabama becomes a big story.

2004- Continued

It is one particular appearance that starts Patti and the zoo on another fateful journey no one would ever believe possible. A few days after the evacuation, Peter Jennings of ABC World News features Patti as his Person of the Week, “…And so we hail Patti Hall…shelter from the storm.” As it happens, Los Angeles documentary TV producer Julie Leifermann watches the segment and makes note of this compelling story.

2005

Six months after the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo has survived Hurricane Ivan, TV Producer Leifermann looks up Patti and the zoo and finds that they are struggling to rebuild the zoo facility, but the animals are all there, happy and healthy. Within weeks, a 13-episode TV series is developed and sold to Animal Planet and Leifermann’s L.A. production company converges on Gulf Shores to bring this heroic and touching tale to a global broadcast audience.

At the start of shooting, they all endure two more evacuations for Hurricanes Dennis and Katrina, but Patti and her staff are determined, in spite of setbacks, to complete the rebuild and reopen the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo.

2006

On February 15th The Little Zoo That Could debuts on primetime TV and America falls in love with Patti Hall, her amazing zookeepers, and about 300 of the most charming zoo animals you could ever meet. Monetary donations pour in as viewers witness the inspiring dedication of Patti and her staff lovingly care for their animals while attempting a comeback of the zoo. Hope turns into triumph and the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo is able to open its doors only 14 months after being completely destroyed. It becomes known as The Little Zoo, a “must-see” place on the map, and tourism comes roaring back to the town of Gulf Shores and its neighboring communities still recovering from the hurricanes. By the end of 2006, the zoo has the most successful season in its history.

2007

Life is still precarious. June to November is hurricane season. The reconstructed zoo sitting atop swampland covered in sand on a barrier island cannot survive another powerful storm. It is a ticking time bomb. The only long-term solution is to move to safer terrain and build a new zoo. An impossibly expensive, complicated dream. But thanks to another Gulf Shores family, this isn’t going to be a far-fetched dream. Animal-lovers Clyde Weir and his daughter Andrea are deeply touched by The Little Zoo TV series and want to help in a big way. 

2007-Continued

They stun Patti with a gift to the zoo of 25 acres of prime Gulf Shores real estate located four miles off the island. However, designing and building a new multi-million dollar facility is a complicated endeavor, and over the ensuing years, the enormous resources and commitments required by a non-profit zoo, make it very difficult. By 2008, The Great Recession adds to this challenge.

2010

The worse man-made disaster to hit the Gulf, the Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill puts Patti’s dream zoo into a deep freeze. The beach communities of Alabama take a devastating hit from the spill, as do their tourism business. Fundraising for a new zoo comes to a grinding halt. Coping with yet another disaster, Patti is determined to keep the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo viable.

2011

In a brilliant attempt to raise awareness about the environmental impact the oil spill had on wildlife, the new zoo team developed a design concept that would place the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo at the forefront of conservation and sustainability as a fully operational green zoo. But again, their efforts to raise enough capital were hampered by slow economic recovery. This ambitious plan was not to be. But as they always did under Patti’s leadership, they re-grouped and continued to build on the current zoo’s success.

2014

An important alliance is made with renowned animal expert Jim Fowler who assists Patti with a more feasible design path for the new zoo. In another amazing twist of fate, Joey Ward, the same person who built Zooland Animal Park meets Jim Fowler. Twenty-seven years later, Wade and Pat Ward financially jumpstart another new zoo construction project.

2016

Joey Ward is overseeing construction of the new Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo in its new location and Patti Hall is on the brink of living her dream - The Little Zoo That Grew, safe and sound, once and for all. Circle of life, indeed.

Join us in fostering a deeper understanding and appreciation for the incredible wildlife that graces our facility.

We can't do it without you.

As a non-profit organization, the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo relies on the generous support of donations to support its mission to create compelling experiences that connect people and community with wildlife, and inspire personal responsibility for conservation of the natural world.

Your Donations to the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo allow the zoo to:
Provide Daily Animal Care – fresh diets, healthcare (vet visits, medications), clean habitats
Provide Enrichment – Enrichment = Happiness. Toys, puzzle feeders, boomer balls keep animals curious, active, and mentally engaged
Provide Habitat Upgrades – climbing structures, pools, perching, ropes, and regular maintenance are critical to healthy habitats
Provide Community Education – By sharing the importance of the animals at the zoo, the community learns about conservation and how to protect our environment

Every donation makes an immediate impact for the animals that call the zoo home. 

Select your donation amount below and carefully choose a selection for a one-time gift or recurring (weekly, monthly, quarterly).

When we close our gates at the end of each day, we are still hard at work caring for animals, maintaining the facility, preparing and planning what comes next in the life of a non-profit zoo that operates 365 days a year, come rain or shine, no matter what the circumstances.

Each holiday season, the Zoo hosts its Animal Caring Tree to support the animals and care teams through the leaner season. 

Support the Animal Caring Tree this holiday season by visiting https://ZooCaringTree.givesmart.com.

LEARN WITH US
Inspiring Education & Conservation

What better way to learn about animals and how we humans can become better stewards of Earth’s wildlife than visiting a zoo? The animals of the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo are the cornerstone and inspiration for every educational program we offer.

With over 200 animals, there couldn’t be better learning opportunities: for families, school groups, and community or organization events for anyone interested in the wonderful creatures we share this planet with.

Avenues For Learning
School Groups &
Educational Programs

Bring your classroom to the wild with our School Groups & Educational Programs at the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo! Our free curriculum-based lesson plans provide students with hands-on learning opportunities that spark curiosity and inspire a love for wildlife.

Reserve your educational adventure today and turn learning into an unforgettable experience!

We offer a discounted admission rate for a minimum of 15 students and chaperones.

$10 per student
$8 per chaperone
Teachers, support staff, and bus drivers are free.
 

There is a 10-person minimum for daycare groups.

Reservations are required. 

Don’t Forget To Add An Educational Program: 

$50 additional fee for up to 25 students
$80 additional fee for over 26 students.
Bring the Zoo to You! Ambassador Programs

Experience the adventure of the zoo up close with our Bring the Zoo to You Ambassador Program! 

Designed to educate and inspire, this outreach initiative brings our animal ambassadors and expert zookeepers directly to schools, libraries, community centers, special events, and more.

Our engaging presentations showcase incredible animals while highlighting conservation, animal behavior, and the vital role zoos play in protecting wildlife. 

Our local communities play a very important role in life at the Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo! Book a visit and let us bring the adventure of the zoo to you!

Under the guidance of our keepers, we’re able to engage each participant and teach them about the animal species in its natural habitat and status in the wild, its life at the zoo, and so much more.

Get Up Close!
All adventures are weather permitting.
Destination Madagascar

While visiting Destination: Madagascar, you are transported into the home of our black and white ring tailed lemurs. You will have the opportunity to meet these unusual animals from the Island of Madagascar and learn about their environment. Join us at Destination: Madagascar to learn more about these critically endangered animals.

LEARN MORE
South American Adventure

In the South American Adventure, you will walk along a boardwalk in the “jungle” to discover and meet a variety of animals from the tropical rainforests of Central and South America. During this adventure, you will learn about tortoises, macaws, sloths, and the importance of tropical forests in our everyday lives. Join us for a South American Adventure!

LEARN MORE
Giraffe
Feedings

Did you know the word “twiga” means giraffe in Swahili?  At the Twiga Station, you can meet our giraffes, learn about them, and have a chance to feed one of them!  These gentle giants eat as much as 70 pounds of leaves a day.  Help the keepers by feeding the giraffes various types of browse.  Be sure to check out their amazingly long tongues!

Tickets are now on sale for Art on the Wild Side: Wine & Whiskey Stroll, the annual spring fundraiser benefiting your local nonprofit Alabama Gulf Coast Zoo.

Guests (21+) are invited to enjoy an unforgettable evening on Saturday, March 28, 2026, strolling through the zoo while sampling fine wines, craft whiskeys, and gourmet bites surrounded by your favorite animal ambassadors. Guests will have the opportunity to meet animal ambassadors and experience animal training demonstrations.

Art on the Wild Side begins with an online auction on March 21, which includes one-of-a-kind, unique pieces of art created by the zoo animals. Whether painted with paws, claws, fur, footprints, or nose boops, each piece is a true masterpiece. The auction also includes vacation packages, golf outings, and more, generously donated by local businesses and community members.

As a local non-profit organization, the support from this event is critical to helping provide care and enrichment to the animals that call the zoo home. This includes fresh diets, healthcare, habitats that include climbing structures, perching, ropes, and more that keep each animal from the smallest hedgehog to the largest lion healthy, active and mentally engaged.

Your support also helps the zoo provide hands-on conservation education and programs throughout the community that continue the Zoo’s mission of connecting people of all ages with wildlife and encouraging them to protect the world around them.

Tickets to the annual fundraiser are $125 per person, and $100 per person for Zoo Members. Sponsorship packages are available and include varying levels of benefits. Click here to purchase tickets and for more information.

Special thanks to Visionary Sponsors Dr. Mike and Janet Asher and the City of Orange Beach.
